authoredFrom: Why a separate expectation: normal-delivery.trip.expected.json describes one uninterrupted consumer. Here the transport of normal-delivery.json gets a second durable connection at 606 ms, and the first commit of job.delivered (eventSeq 8) fails once inside its transaction with SQLITE_FULL (DISK_FULL) or SQLITE_BUSY (DATABASE_LOCKED), both retryable (E7); the same service reconnects and the producer redelivers 8.

Events 1-7 commit as in normal-delivery: trip@3 opens partial with opened-at-load (T12) with truck 1 and trailer 2, and observed distance 0 m is persisted at eventSeq 5 (T16). The failed commit rolls back event 8 and its effects; the recorder keeps its state (T3).

The reconnection is stepped at the session open (R6): the not-connected interval runs from the last committed item (eventSeq 7: label 1,800,000,000,500, source time 1,000,500,000,000 ns) to the second welcome's capture (atMs 606: 1,000,606,000,000 ns) on the capture clock; the trip is already partial, so no trip.update. Both readings around the hole (the snapshot at 200 and the second checkpoint) report odometer 1,000,500 m for the same truck, so odometerDeltaM is 0 (T16).

The redelivered job.delivered carries the queued interval first, then attribution trip and the close {delivered, outcome, partial} at 1,800,000,000,600. The live job.cleared (9) adds nothing. Nine first commits, no duplicate.
